Hi Tom / Ava —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap of what we heard and the concrete levers we discussed so your team can validate against internal budgets and procurement gates. Short TL;DR at the top, details below.

TL;DR: primary pain is token spend for near-real-time auth and fraud scoring (~3–4M tokens/day). Two high-impact levers we can pilot: (1) per-request batching + micro-batching at the gateway (likely 15–25% token savings for scoring patterns), and (2) prefix/KV caching for repeated context (30–45% savings on long session flows). Together we estimate 35–55% unit-cost reduction for the scoring workload depending on hit rates.

Key pain points you raised
- Cost volatility during peak churn windows (midnight ET batch jobs + spikes from onboarding flows)
- Need to keep tail latency < 120ms for scoring calls to avoid product regressions
- Procurement budget ceiling for Q4: $25k–$40k/month depending on SLA needs

Goals we sketched
1) Demonstrate 30–40% token-cost reduction on production-like traffic in a 4-week pilot.
2) Keep p95 latency within 120–150ms; route to lower-cost model variants only on capacity pressure (no user-visible errors).
3) Surface per-route token and latency dashboards in Redwood Console for 30-day window.

Levers & assumptions (initial model)
- Batching: continuous batching with 8–16ms enqueue budget; effective batch size depends on concurrency pattern. We modeled a typical scoring throughput and saw 15–25% token reduction because of request aggregation and fewer repeated prefix tokens.
- KV/Prefix caching: for onboarding flows and similar users, we assumed a 40% cache hit rate on average; this yields 30–45% token reduction for those flows.
- Quantization & model variants: switching to int8-ish variant saves ~20% GPU cost but adds ~10–12% quality delta; we only recommend it for lower-sensitivity routes.

Estimated unit economics (sample scenarios)
- Conservative: 25% average token savings -> projected bill reduction to ~$30k/month (from baseline ~$40k)
- Aggressive: 45% average token savings -> projected bill reduction to ~$22k/month

Attachments: I attached a quick model (RDW-token-econ-quickmodel.xlsx) with the assumptions we used, and a one-page mutual action plan (Clearflow-MAP-v1.docx) outlining milestones.

Next steps / asks for Clearflow
1) Confirm the hard budget gate for pilot (is $25k/month a firm ceiling or is there flexibility up to $40k with an SLA add-on?).
2) Share a representative 24–48h trace or logs (anonymized) so our SREs can refine batching assumptions. Drive link or S3 works.
3) If procurement requires an MSA/PO prior to pilot, share the timeline or the procurement contact and we’ll loop Legal.

Proposed Redwood pilot scope (4 weeks) — high level- Week 0: baseline telemetry + small traffic mirror- Week 1: enable batching + observe impact on tokens/latency- Week 2: enable prefix caching for targeted routes- Week 3: stabilize + produce cost report and dashboard

I’ll wait to hear which budget gate you prefer and whether procurement wants the MSA before kickoff.

- The $25k/month is the preferred cap from Product/Finance for a pilot unless we can show a clear >30% ROI within the first 2 months. Procurement will likely require PO + MSA for anything above $30k.

Tom —
Quick answers to your operational questions:

- Pilot infra and fallbacks: Redwood can run the pilot in a mixed routing policy that keeps a low-latency pool reserved for routes with strict p99 targets. If batching increases p99 beyond the configured guardrail, traffic for those routes will automatically cut over to the reserved pool. That fallback incurs the cost of the reserved pool (which we model separately) but prevents user-visible latency issues.
- Quantized variants: switching to a quantized variant is a config change on our serving runtime when an open model artifact already exists; no separate import is required for standard quantized builds. If you want a specific vetted variant, our Model Ops team can pin it for the pilot.

Sample pricing & pilot options (rough sketches)
A) Budget-first pilot (low-risk): capped at $25k/month, limit to non-critical routes (scoring-batchable flows). Expect ~25–30% token savings in this scope.
B) SLA-first pilot (higher fidelity): $35–40k/month to include reserved low-latency pool + broader route coverage — projected savings 35–45% and stronger p99 guarantees.

If you confirm A vs B I can draft the SOW + MAP and have Rishi run a short sizing job to validate batch hit-rates on your sample traces.

Cheers,
